newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Prosecutors file charges against miners' leader.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors file charges against miners' leader.

text.p: Prosecutors filed charges of undermining state authority on Thursday against miners' leader Miron Cosma in connection with riots which toppled Romania's first post-communist government in 1991.
A spokeswoman for the prosecutor's office said the 107-page indictment had been turned over to Bucharest court. No date has been set for his trial.

Charges also include firearms violations, incitement to violence and compromising rail safety during a six-day rampage which started in western Romania's Jiu Valley mining district and tore through central Bucharest. Cosma faces up to 15 years in jail if convicted.
"The way in which the actions were staged and railway staff forced to breach safety regulations displays organisation of a military-like nature," the indictment read.
Miners upset by ex-prime minister Petre Roman's pro-market austerity measures commandeered trains to Bucharest in 1990 and 1991, smashing buildings and beating up student demonstrators.

The charges relate to the second upheaval in September, 1991, when miners sacked the government building and Roman was forced from office. Cosma denies instigating violence, saying during the investigation that he was only "the instrument of the miners' will".

Romania's new centrist coalition government has pledged to bring to justice those responsible for the violence. During the election campaign that brought him to power last year, President Emil Constantinescu accused his predecessor, ex-communist Ion Iliescu, of encouraging the miners.
Miners denounced his arrest in January, but threatened protests have come to nothing.
